# Synthetic Unity serialized fixtures

Provenance: every byte is generated by `build_fixtures.py` in this folder from literal
values. No Unity editor, game, Unity or I2 Localization assembly, or downloaded template
was used. UnityPy contributes only its bundled Unity 2017.4 class layouts (GameObject,
MonoBehaviour, MonoScript) and its type-tree value writer. The files are licensed with
the repository.

| Fixture | Installed by the tests as | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `typetree.bin` | `Synthetic_Data/sharedassets0.assets` | Format 17, Unity `2017.4.40f1`, type trees present: a GameObject, a local `I2.Loc.LanguageSource` MonoScript and an I2-shaped MonoBehaviour |
| `managed.bin` | `Synthetic_Data/resources.assets` | The same MonoBehaviour bytes without type trees, with an empty component name, plus a non-I2 MonoBehaviour; scripts are external |
| `scripts.bin` | `Synthetic_Data/globalgamemanagers.assets` | The two MonoScripts referenced by `managed.bin` |
| `assembly.bin` | `Synthetic_Data/Managed/Synthetic.I2.dll` | A metadata-only 32-bit .NET image with `I2.Loc` types for the managed fallback; it has no method bodies or entry point and is never loaded or executed |

The committed names avoid the `.assets` and `.dll` suffixes that source packages and
`.gitignore` reserve for real game data; tests copy the files into a temporary game
folder under their installed names.

The I2 source has three languages (`en`, `tr`, `ja`) and five terms in this order:
`Menu/Start`, `Dialog/Intro`, `Fonts/Main` (a font term, not text), `Menu/Empty`
(empty English text) and `Credits`. The assembly also declares a static field, a
`[NonSerialized]` field, private fields with and without `[SerializeField]`, an int32
enum, `List<T>`, `T[]`, `byte[]` and `UnityEngine.Object` references.

Regenerate after changing the builder, then run the tests:

```
.venv/Scripts/python tests/fixtures/unity-serialized/build_fixtures.py
.venv/Scripts/python tests/fixtures/unity-serialized/build_fixtures.py --check
```

`tests/test_unity_worker_e2e.py` fails when the committed bytes differ from the builder
output. Corrupted variants are built by the same functions at test time and are not
committed.
